correctness.rationale: The covering x↦dx reduces both optimizations to coprime r,s and lifts each contact d times. In the reduced problem the derivative of s sin(rx)+r sin(sx) factors as 2rs cos(Sx/2)cos((s−r)x/2). On the sum grid the two sines coincide; r(2j+1) modulo 2S runs over a whole parity class because gcd(r,S)=1. Its residues nearest S/2 have distance 1/2 (one contact), 1 (two contacts), or 0 (one contact), respectively for S odd, S divisible by four, or S congruent to two modulo four. On the difference grid the sines are opposite, so the weighted sum is at most s−r; S(1−c_S)<2≤2r (with S=3 also directly checked) makes this branch strictly suboptimal. Integrating the positive weighted inequality and evaluating at contact atoms proves sharpness and the full measure classification. Evaluation at a contact also bounds any real coefficient pair, and differentiating an equality point gives am=bn when c_S<1. In the c_S=1 case the stated simplex of feasible maximizers gives nonuniqueness without claiming exhaustion. The second derivative at any lifted contact is −mn c_S, giving the stated local coefficient; strict inequality off the finite contact set and compactness give the global quadratic gap and the integrated concentration estimate. The uploaded checker was read only; finite regressions are not used as proof.

value.rationale: A natural sparse version of an established sine optimization has a complete sharp classification governed only by the reduced frequency sum. The divisibility-by-four branch changes not just the constant but the number of optimizing atoms and hence uniqueness of the probability law.
